# Notes

This page tells how the `notes` slice of the core plugin `claudetto` works.
A user reads it to learn what a note above the prompt means and how to use its keys.
A contributor reads it before an edit of `slices/notes/`.
The slice makes no model call, so a note adds no request and no token to a turn.

## What It Does for You

A note is one line above the prompt, such as `Repeated deny · Bash(rm:*) stopped 3 calls`.
It stays for 2 prompts.
Only one note shows at a time, and a newer note replaces the older one.

## Where Notes Come From

- The same permission deny or ask three times in one session. The note names the rule and the settings file that holds it.
- The same check command fails three times in a row with the same failing test. The note names the test and the count.
- A `learn:` block at the end of a main reply. The reply gives a `learn:` line, a `tag:` line, and an `explain:` block.
  The slice hides the block in the reply and shows `<tag> · <line>`.
  `learn: none` shows nothing.
- The `Stop` hook of [Finish](Finish), for a reply that defers work or says done with no proof.

## Keys

| Key | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `1` | Puts "Here is a note offered by a side agent:" and the note with its explanation into the prompt box. |
| `2` | Turns notes off. |
| `3` | Shows when notes are off, and turns them on again. |

The keys work while the band above the prompt has the focus, and `1` also works in an empty prompt box.

## Back-Off and Dedupe

When you type past `n` notes in a row, the slice skips the next `2^(n-3)` notes for `n` of 3 or more, up to `SKIP_MAX` (16).
A note whose line matches one of the last `RECENT_MAX` (50) lines shows nothing.
Using the insert key ends the run of ignored notes.

## Background Task and User Edit

- A background task in flight for 30 minutes (`BACKGROUND_MS`). The API gives no start time and no output time of a task.
  So at each `Stop` the slice records the first time that it saw each ID of `background_tasks`, drops the IDs that are gone, and tells once per task.
  The rule counts the time in flight alone, and a task that prints output still gets the note.
- A user edit in a file that the agent edits next. At an allowed `Edit` or `Write`, the slice runs `git status` for the file.
  When it shows a change and no line of the edit ledger of `hygiene` holds the hash of the file now, the note says that Claude did not make the change.

## Hooks

| Hook | Filter | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool.check` | `Bash`, `Edit`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Read`, `WebFetch`, `Write` | Counts denies and asks by rule, and checks an `Edit` or `Write` for a change of the user. |
| `classic.Stop` | `hook_event_name: "Stop"` | Records the background tasks and tells of one in flight for 30 minutes. |
| `classic.PostToolUseFailure` | `Bash` | Counts a failing check command. |
| `classic.PostToolUse` | `Bash` | A passed check ends its streak. |
| `turn.step` | `turnId` (each step) | Removes the `learn:` block from the shown and stored text of a main reply, and reads its note. |
| `turn.complete` | None | Takes the note of `finish`. |
| `turn.start` | None | Ages the shown note at each typed prompt of the main loop. |
| `ui.render` | `AbovePrompt` | Draws the note and its keys. |
| `ui.render` | `AssistantMessage` | Hides the `learn:` block. |
